Government chatbots have become increasingly popular as artificial-intelligence-based tools to improve communication between the government and its citizens. This study explores the interaction mode design of a trustworthy government chatbot, which involves multiple social characteristics from the user-centric perspective. A discrete choice experiment was conducted in the context of Chinese government chatbots to examine the effects of various social characteristics on citizen preferences. Participants utilized a crowdsourcing survey platform to report their preferences for interaction processes designed with distinct sets of social characteristics. Valid data were obtained from 371 participants and analyzed using a multinomial logit model. The results indicate that (in order from highest to lowest impact) emotional intelligence, proactivity, identity consistency, and conscientiousness significantly influence the citizens’ preferences. Identity consistency has a negative effect, whereas the other factors all have positive impacts. It was also determined that some of these correlations are influenced by the participants ’ individual characteristics, such as age, gender, and prior experience with chatbots. This work provides empirical evidence for the relative importance of social characteristics and their impacts on user perception, expands the service dimension scope of information provision/communication (one of five categories of digital interaction), and facilitates the identification and operationalization of the social characteristics. We provide a theoretical framework to understand the interaction model design of a trustworthy government chatbot and also offer practical recommendations for government chatbot designers and policy implications.

　カインさん(現姓Ｃｈｉｋｉｍａさん）から「凄いところがあるよ～」と教えてもらったＨＰを見てびっくり仰天。
　岐阜県北部のダイナランドスキー場で仮装大賞なるものが開かれているとか。

　「コスプレあり、アニメキャラあり、着ぐるみあり・・・。 思いっきり仮装して、ゲレンデで楽しく目立った人には、『仮装パフォーマンス大賞』を贈ります。そして賞品は今年も海外旅行！シーズン中、ユニークなファッションをしてスキー、スノーボードを滑った方の中から投票により3 名に、豪華商品をプレゼント！投票者からも抽選で3名に豪華商品をプレゼント！」

　と書かれているではありませんか。
　実のところ、以前からアスカでスキーしてみたらおもしろいだろうなと思っていたのですが、スキー場の許可等を考えると、そうは出来るものではないなと考えあぐねていた矢先だったのです。
　振り向きざま、例の邪悪な笑顔で「チャ～ンス！」と言ったとか、言わなかったとか・・・・

　でも、既に２月中旬まではアレコレ予定が入ってしまっていたり、一緒に行こうとしていたドーラー仲間も諸般の事情で行けなくなり・・・。で、結局着ぐるスキーを決行したのはスキーシーズンも後半の２／２６となってしまいました。この日、しのさん、笹原さんにサポートをお願いして、アスカはただ１人着ぐるスキーに挑戦したのでした。


　　ここからはＢＧＭにエヴァンゲリオン・サウンドトラックの「ＥＶＡ－０２」を聞きながら見て下さい（ｗ


　ＡＳＵＫＡ　ＳＴＲＩＫＥ！　

ゲレンデに立てば注目の的。

　(何分古い写真なので画質はご容赦を)

リフトで口説かれてたり・・・　（＾＾；）　　

「・・・・アスカ、行くわよ！」　　　　

　覚悟を決めて滑りだすと・・・・思っていたよりは、ちゃんと滑れましたね。着ぐるみで滑るときに困るのが、まず雪面がよく見えないこと。視界の狭さは気になりませんが、目の部分は紗になっているので、雪面の凸凹がほとんど見えないんです。ですから、パラレルターンはまずムリ。無理に滑ったら、たちまちエッジをとられてひっくり返るでしょう。シンジならともかく、アスカですっころんでいたんじゃ、イイ笑い者。それだけは避けないと。で、直滑降＋シュテムターンで滑ることに。これならなんとか滑れました。

　滑るときはしのさんと笹原さんが後に先に滑ってくれてサポート。時に並行して滑りながら写真撮ってくれたりして、感謝、感謝です。ここの画像はしのさん、笹原さんが撮ってくれた写真です。サイズがまばらなのはこのお二方＋ＴＡＫＡのデジカメの計３台のカメラで撮ったり、ハガキサイズプリントされたものだったりのせいです（＾＾；）
　滑ってる合間にも、「一緒に写真撮ってくれませんか？」とか「加持さんはどうしたのかな？」とか、あちこちから声をかけていただいて、これらもとっても楽しかったです。小さなお子さんも、結構アスカを知ってましたね。握手してあげたり、頭さすってあげると、とっても喜んでくれていました。

　ちょっとひとやすみ。写真ではわかりにくいけど、左はオバケのＱちゃんです。

何見てんのよ～！

アスカで計４本滑って、２時間くらいゲレンデにいましたがとっても楽しい、あっという間の２時間でした。プラグスーツの下にゼンタイを着込んでいたこともあって、スキー中もそんなに寒くはなかったです。プラグスーツはスキーウエア代わりにも十分なっていました。逆に言うと、どうりで夏のコミケではサウナスーツになってしまうわけですねー。
　ですが日も暮れてきて、いよいよ雪面も見えなくなってきたので、惜しみつつもゲレンデにお別れしたのでした。

　白銀のアスカ　　　　　　
　この写真は私一番のお気に入り。笹原さん撮影です。さすが、元プロカメラマン。

さて、そんなわけで、ダイナランドで無事着ぐるみスキーをやってまいりました。
　そして、現地で仮装パフォーマンス大賞の係りの方にも写真を撮っていただいてエントリーしてまいりました。
　エントリー受付自体はスキーシーズン始まってから３／１２の締め切りまででした。アスカがエントリーしたのは２／２６ですから、もう投票も後半押し迫った頃でした。「別に大賞にはならなくてもいいから、上位に入って着ぐるみがＰＲできたら・・・」と思ってました。けれど、エントリーしたのは２／２６だったのですが、ダイナランドのＨＰ上にアスカが掲示されたのがなんと３／６！締め切りまでたった７日しかない。（が～ん）
　スキーシーズン１００日以上ある中、たった７日間の投票だけで戦うなんて、絶望的な戦いじゃない。これじゃ、上位どころか、その他大勢で埋もれてしまうかも。うう、やっぱアスカって悲劇のヒロイン！（爆）

　でも、投票始まったら凄かったですね。たった３日で２位にまで浮上して、途中エントリー名「ひまわり」さんと抜きつ抜かれつもしましたが、結局２位でゴールインしちゃいました。１位の「復習のメロディ」さんはダントツ悠々１位でしたね。投票のシステムが「１位になった人に投票した方にも抽選でプレゼントを差し上げる」となっていたので、先に１位を走っていた復讐のメロディさんに票が集中してしまうようになっていて、加速度的に票が増えていくシステムになっていたんです。でも、それを差し引いたら、アスカは１位にはならなかったけど、大善戦だったなって思ってます（メジャーなキャラ強し）。それと、メタモルフォーゼ研究所のチャット仲間の応援も絶大でしたね。皆さんホントにありがとう（＾＾）

　しかし、更に後日談があります。
　勝敗はどう転ぶことやら。受付終了後の発表ではアスカは３位でした。大賞はレインボー＆ビンボーさん、２位はカップルプードルさん、そして、復習のメロディさんはインタネット特別賞でした。大賞はネット投票とゲレンデ得票とによって決まるのだそうで。カップルプードルさんはかなり早くからエントリーしてたので、ゲレンデ得票数が多そうなのは分かるんですが、アスカより更に遅れてエントリーして、ネット投票に１度も上位に出なかった組が大賞になったのです。・・・・ほえ？
　これには、ちょっと首をひねってます。３／９～１０日のたった二日で上位三名をブッちぎってネット投票数が急に増えているのも、なにかヘンですよね？？？

　・・・まぁ、あんまりそういうことこだわるより、ゲレンデで遊べたことで良しとしておこう。うん！
　
（注）
　今回着ぐるみでスキーをしたのはパフォーマンス大会の許可を得てやっています。
　また、アスカのスキー滑走前には先行サポートが滑って雪面を確認し、アスカ滑走時は併走してサポートも滑り、周囲にして細心の注意を払っています。
　スキーは普通に滑っても激突、巻き込まれ、あるいは転倒による事故があります。
　視界と動きに制約がかかる着ぐるみでは危険が倍加します。
　もしあなたもやるとしたら、スキー場の許可は必ず得た上で、万全を期して欲しいです。"

Considering the significance of the Western Zhou oracle bone inscriptions in understanding the religious thought and practices of the time, the following future research directions can be proposed to help expand our knowledge on this subject:

1. Technological advancements: Utilizing advanced technologies and innovative methods, such as digital imaging or artificial intelligence, to decipher, analyze, and reconstruct the oracle bone inscriptions, could lead to a more in-depth understanding of the underlying religious practices and thought of the Western Zhou period.

2. Interdisciplinary approaches: Employing interdisciplinary approaches, such as anthropology, archaeology, linguistics, and religious studies, can provide a more integrated and holistic insight into the Western Zhou religious thought and practices.

3. Semantic analysis: Conducting a semantic analysis of the inscriptions, focusing on the meaning and significance of the symbols and characters used, can contribute to deciphering the complex religious language and symbolism of the era, revealing deeper layers of meaning and understanding.

4. 5. Impact on modern religious practices: Exploring the impact of Western Zhou religious thought on contemporary Chinese religious practices can assist in identifying any continued legacy of these ancient beliefs in the current religious landscape, thereby highlighting the ongoing importance and relevance of these early religious ideas.

Conclusion:

Western Zhou oracle bone inscriptions remain an invaluable resource for understanding the religious thought and practices of ancient China. By adopting a diverse range of research methodologies and exploring various interrelated aspects, future investigations can significantly enrich our understanding of this formative period in Chinese history. The potential insights gained from such research will not only shed light on the religious beliefs and practices of the Western Zhou period but also contribute to a broader and more comprehensive understanding of the development and impact of these ideas throughout Chinese history and across different cultural contexts. The dissemination of Confucian classics and culture in Europe in the 18th century had a significant impact on the philosophical and intellectual development of Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz, a German philosopher and mathematician. Leibniz’s interest in Confucianism was sparked by his belief that the discovery and dissemination of new ideas was essential for the advancement of human knowledge and understanding. He saw in Confucianism a philosophy that had much to contribute to the development of European thought, particularly in terms of social harmony and personal morality.

One of the key aspects of Confucianism that Leibniz found particularly appealing was its focus on the importance of mutual respect and tolerance for different cultures and traditions. He believed that this was essential for the creation of a more harmonious and just society, one in which people could learn from each other and work together for the common good. Leibniz saw Confucianism as an alternative to the aggressive and intolerant attitudes that were prevalent in Europe at the time, and he hoped that its teachings could help to promote a more open and inclusive approach to intellectual inquiry.

In addition to his interest in Confucianism as a moral and social philosophy, Leibniz was also fascinated by the more practical aspects of Chinese culture, such as the development of printing techniques and the use of algebraic notation. He saw in these innovations a glimpse of a more efficient and effective way of organizing human knowledge, which he hoped could be applied to the study of mathematics and other sciences in Europe.

Overall, the impact of the dissemination of Confucian classics and culture on Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz was significant and far-reaching. Through his engagement with Confucianism, Leibniz helped to promote a more open and inclusive approach to intellectual inquiry, and he contributed to the development of new philosophical and mathematical ideas that continue to shape our understanding of the world today.

Translate to spanish:
In the early hours of dawn, when the mist still clung to the grass and dew sparkled like a bed of silver coins, the gates of the Castle Fairhaven creaked open. Two cloaked figures emerged, the hems of their garments sweeping across the cobblestones. The taller of the two was a man named Eamon, whose eyes carried secrets older than the castle itself. Beside him, a smaller figure moved with purpose, wrapped tight in her own cloak - this was the fiery Marielle.

The sun hung low and orange on the horizon, letting shadows spill across the world and pool into the same darkness as the secret they shared.

“Day’s first light, Marielle,” Eamon began, his breathes casting puffs of mist in the morning air. “A fitting time for the great revelation.” He motioned to the parchment clutched tightly in the girl’s hands. She barely acknowledged it, and her eyes remained fixed upon the distance as if she sought some far-off certainty.

“Of course, Eamon,” Marielle replied with forced patience, entwining her fingers in the hem of her cloak. “It’s just that we must be discreet. Father’s wrath knows no bounds, and I fear the consequences if he discovers what we’re about to do.”

Now it was Eamon who hesitated, sensing the weight of destiny settling in the lines around his eyes. “Marielle,” he said solemnly, “I must tread lightly and ask: is your heart sure of this path? We may yet turn back, and no one would be the wiser.”

At last, her gaze fell upon him, her eyes dancing like twin embers in the gray morning. “Recall Queen Nalíni’s tale, Eamon: how she defied her own father for the sake of love? It is my fate, too, to challenge mine,” she said quietly, determination blossoming on her white cheeks. “For what is a kingdom with a heart that withers in the cold embrace of duty?”

Eamon bowed his head, no more words to be spoken. The city gave a waking stretch around them, and Marielle tucked the parchment safely beneath her cloak. Their quest began in earnest.

They traversed the marble streets that wound through houses and shops as the magic began to stir in the air. Magic, ancient and wild, held dominion on this land, and sunlight whispered secrets to the shadows.

The reveal of Marielle’s secret would no doubt send shockwaves through the soul of the kingdom: a spellbinding tale written in luminous characters that glinted like sunrise on steel. Of love, sacrifice, and the clash of power poised to set the world aflame.

The city gradually surrendered itself to the unspoiled wilds beyond. Their path wended its way between ancient and gnarled trees crowned with a canopy that seemed to choke out the sun itself. Slowly the air grew hushed, laden with the whispers of spells long-silent, and the murmurs of untamed power echoing through the undergrowth.

But today would not be the day for silence, nor the day for secrets. Today, fate would have its way, come flame or fury, and it would not be deterred.

Marielle and Eamon reached the sacred grove, and there they would reveal the secret that would change the course of history. As they prepared themselves for the dust of destiny to claim them, Eamon took one last look at the girl he had long protected, and his voice carried a gravity that would have snapped weaker branches.

“Go forth, Marielle,” he said, “and shatter your chains. For it is within your birthright to set your heart ablaze and seize the future.”

The parchment trembled in her grasp, and her eyes were bright with the flames of her soul that sought release. With a nod, Marielle stepped into the grove, her heart beating a song of ancient heroes, a battle cry against the old order.

And so, the sun rose on a new day in the Kingdom of Fairhaven, a day of change and of courage written in the timeless hand of fate.

translate following for IELTS writing task 2 with score expectation over than 8: 人们常常对是否应该赋予孩子额外的责任而争论不休，比如是否应该要求他们课余时间帮助家务劳动或者一些工作相关的任务，或者是否应该允许他们在学校环境之外随心所欲的度过闲暇时间。在这篇文章中，我将对两种观点进行讨论，并提出我自己对这个问题的看法。 一方面，支持赋予孩子们额外责任的人们认为，给孩子分配课外责任可以尽早培养对时间管理和职业道德重要性的意识。通过协助家务劳动或者帮助完成合适的工作任务，孩子们可以学习基本的职业技能，特别是团队合作、面对难题时的解决方案和心态调整以及努力工作的价值认同。此外，拥有责任感可以培养孩子的自豪感和成就感，从而增强他们的自尊心，这些品质往往在一个人的成功中不可或缺。而且，让孩子参与家庭的日常工作也能加强家庭内部的团结意识。 而另一方面，相反观点的支持者断言，应该让孩子在学业之外尽可能享受童年的自由。这是因为，年轻人正处于人生重要决断的早起，需要更多的时间去发掘自己的兴趣以及自己的才能所在，这对他们未来的个人发展和人生决策有着至关重要的作用。而且，参加体育、艺术等休闲活动抑或是与朋友共度时光，也有助于孩子的情绪健康和精神放松，这与在学业方面的成功同等重要。此外，通过有更多的时间沉浸在各种愉快的体验中，孩子们能更好的应对生活中的挑战以适应不断变换的环境。 于我而言，在两种观点中保持一种适当的平衡是孩子培养过程中更为理想的一种方式。诚然让孩子尽早的具备责任感和发展基本的生活技能至关重要，但是我们也应当注意到每个人个人兴趣和整体心理健康的重要性。给予与年龄相匹配的任务并留出时间进行休闲活动的灵活安排对年轻人大有裨益，因为这不仅使他们意识到努力工作的价值，同时也有助于他们自我探索和享受生活的乐趣。 总之，无论是分配额外的责任，还是让孩子享受校外的生活，都各有优点。因此，考虑个人需求和兴趣的平衡才是最有可能为儿童成长提供更全面机会的思考方向。

Please tranlate the following into Chinese: The production of shale gas depends not only on shale resources and capital investment but also on having a flexible and stable policy environment. This paper examines whether and how partisan ideology affects the extraction of shale gas. We use panel fixed effects as well as the system–generalized method of moments approach with quarterly panel data from 15 US states over the period 2007−2016. We consider not only the political ideology of the state governor but also the state legislature’s influence on the governor, control over the governorship and the legislature by the same party, the reelection of an incumbent government, and turnover in the political party in power. The results indicate that because the right-leaning party is more likely to support shale gas development, when a member of that party heads the state government, shale gas production performance is higher than when the left-leaning party is in power. Therefore, the production of shale gas rises with a turnover in political control from left to right, reelection of a right-leaning incumbent, and more right-leaning power in the state legislature. Title: The Influence and Role of the Shang People’s Worship of Cheng Tang: Insights from Oracle Bone Inscriptions

Abstract:
The oracle bone inscriptions reveal that Cheng Tang, the founder of the Shang dynasty, held a significant position in the minds of the Shang people. This paper aims to explore the influence and role of the Shang people’s worship of Cheng Tang based on the oracle bone inscriptions. We examine the various ways in which the Shang kings showed their respect for Cheng Tang, including group ancestor worship, joint sacrifices with other ancestors, and frequent grandiose sacrifices using large numbers of animals and cattle. Furthermore, we analyze the significance of Cheng Tang as a protector of both agriculture and war for the Shang people, considering the specific prayers made to him for a bountiful harvest and victory in war with neighboring states. The findings illustrate the deep-rooted and integral role that Cheng Tang played in the Shang people’s religious and cultural values.

Introduction:
The Shang dynasty is one of the earliest recorded periods of Chinese history, and its religious beliefs have been extensively studied through oracle bone inscriptions. The oracle bone inscriptions provide us with valuable insights into religious practices, beliefs, and the role of gods and ancestors in the Shang culture. Among the various deities worshipped by the Shang people, Cheng Tang held a special place in their religious history. The oracle bone inscriptions elaborate on the reverence accorded to Cheng Tang by the Shang kings and the role he played as a protector of the Shang people.

Reverence towards Cheng Tang:
The Shang kings often conducted group ancestor worship, and Cheng Tang was given a prestigious position as the first ancestor to be worshipped. The joint sacrifices with other ancestors also included Cheng Tang, and these sacrificial offerings were often grandiose, involving a large number of animals and cattle. Such extravagant offerings exemplify the immense respect accorded to Cheng Tang.

Cheng Tang as a Protector:
Cheng Tang was revered as a protector of both agriculture and war. The Shang people frequently prayed to Cheng Tang for a bountiful harvest and victory in war with neighboring states. The role of Cheng Tang as a protector was also highlighted through the numerous rituals and ceremonies associated with his worship. These rituals and ceremonies highlight the importance of Cheng Tang as a protector of the Shang people.

Conclusion:
The worship of Cheng Tang was an integral part of the Shang people’s religious and cultural values. He was revered as a protector of both agriculture and war, and his importance was evident in the various ways in which the Shang kings showed their respect for him through grandiose sacrifices and joint sacrifices with other ancestors. The reverence towards Cheng Tang sheds light on the religious practices and values of the Shang dynasty. The oracle bone inscriptions are a valuable resource for understanding the cultural legacy of the Shang people and their worship of Cheng Tang.

"One moment of perfect beauty."

Listen to the flute how it tells a tale,
complaining of separations—
Saying, “Ever since I was parted from the reed-bed,
my lament, has caused man and woman to moan.
I want a bosom torn by severance,
that I may unfold the pain of love-desire.
Everyone who is left far from his source
wishes back the time when he was united with it.
In every company I uttered my grieving cry;
I consorted with the unhappy and with them that rejoice.
Every one became my friend from his own opinion;
none sought out my secrets from within me.
My secret is not far from my complaint,
but ear and eye lack the light.
Body is not veiled from soul, or soul from body,
yet none is permitted to see the soul.
This noise of the flute is fire, it is not wind:
whoever has not this fire, may he be nothing!
It is the fire of Love that is in the flute,
it is the fervour of Love that is in the wine.
The flute is the comrade of everyone who has been parted from a friend: its strains pierced our hearts.
Who ever saw a poison and antidote like the flute?
Who ever saw a sympathiser and a longing lover like the flute?
The flute tells of the Way full of blood
and recounts stories of the passion of Majnun.
Only to the senseless is this sense confided:
the tongue has no customer save the ear.
In our woe the days have become untimely:
our days travel hand in hand with burning griefs.
If our days are gone, let them go!—It is no matter.
Do You remain, for none is holy as You are!
Whoever is not a fish becomes sated with His water;
whoever is without daily bread finds the day long.
None that is raw understands the state of the ripe:
therefore my words must be brief. Farewell!
O son, burst your chains and be free!
How long will you be a bondsman toe silver and gold?
If you pour the sea into a pitcher, how much will it hold?
One day’s store.
The pitcher, the eye of the covetous, never becomes full:
the oyster-shell is not filled with pearls, until it is contented.
He whose garment is rent by a love
is purged of covetousness and all defect.
Hail, O Love that bring us good gain, 
you that are the physician of all our ills
The remedy of our pride and vainglory,
our Plato and our Galen!
Through Love the earthly body soared to the skies:
the mountain began to dance and became nimble.
Love inspired Mount Sinai, O lover,
Sinai drunk and Moses fell in a swoon.
Were I joined to the lip of one in accord with me,
I too, like the flute, would tell all that may be told;
Whoever is separated from one who speaks his language becomes dumb, though he have a hundred songs.
When the rose is gone and the garden faded,
you will hear no more the nightingale’s story.
The Beloved is all and the lover a veil;
the Beloved is living and the lover a dead thing.
When Love has no care for him, he is left as a bird without wings. Alas for him then!
How should I have consciousness before or behind
when the light of my Beloved is not before me and behind?
Love wills that this Word should be shown forth:
if the mirror does not reflect, how is that?
Do you know why the mirror reflects nothing?
Because the rust is not cleared from its face.

Based on the analysis of the 30 examples of Western Zhou oracle bone inscriptions, there are several implications for further study, which would help deepen our understanding of the religious practices and beliefs during this period:

1. Comparative analysis: With a growing pool of available oracle bone inscriptions from subsequent periods, such as the Eastern Zhou, it would be beneficial to conduct a comparative analysis to understand the continuity and changes in religious thought over time.

2. 4. 5. Cross-cultural analysis: Comparisons between Western Zhou religious thought and those of other ancient civilizations would help contribute to a better understanding of the similarities and differences in ancient religious practices globally.

Conclusion:

The Western Zhou oracle bone inscriptions can offer valuable insights into the religious thought and practices during this formative period in Chinese history. By examining a wide range of inscriptions from various aspects of life, further research can help shed light on the intersection of religion with politics, social structures, and broader cultural developments. Delving deeper into the Western Zhou religious thought and its influence on subsequent generations will enable us to better understand the roots of Chinese civilization and its essential components. Title: Ancestral Gods and Their Offspring in Shang Dynasty Oracle Bone Inscriptions: An Examination of Reasons and Impacts

Abstract
Oracle bone inscriptions serve as a crucial source for understanding the Shang Dynasty’s (c.16th-11th century BCE) complex relationship with ancestral gods. This paper investigates instances where ancestral gods appeared to cause harm to their offspring through the lens of oracle-bone inscriptions. We examine reasons for such harm from the perspective of Shang society, assess the impact on the people’s way of life, and provide an analysis of 20 scholarly references to support our hypotheses.

Introduction
The Shang Dynasty was deeply rooted in ancestral power and worship, with the belief that their deceased ancestors wielded significant influence over their daily lives. Ancestral gods were believed to cause harm or bestow blessings depending on various factors. Though oracle bone inscriptions provide a wealth of information on this subject, there are instances where ancestral gods are portrayed as harming their offspring. This paper will discuss the potential reasons and impacts of such instances, shed light on the complexities of the Shang society’s relationship with their ancestors, and demonstrate the nuances of their religious beliefs and practices.

Main Body

Reasons for Ancestral Gods Causing Harm:
1. Displeasure and punishment: Ancestral gods might display discontent with their descendants due to a lack of proper rituals, sacrifices, or immoral behavior (Keightley, 1978; Liu & Chen, 2012). They could inflict harm to encourage adherence to traditions and moral principles (Yuan, 2006).
2. Ancestors as intermediaries: Communication with deities might happen through ancestral intermediaries (Chang, 1983). In some cases, other gods might have been the source of harm rather than the ancestors themselves (Cao, 1994).
3. Misinterpretation of natural events: Shang people may have attributed natural disasters and illnesses to the wrath of their ancestors, though these events might result from environmental factors unrelated to ancestral influence (Bagley, 2004; Wu, 2011).

Impacts of Ancestral Gods Harming Offspring:
1. Enhancement of ancestor worship: The belief that ancestral gods could harm descendants reinforced the importance of proper rituals and sacrifices, strengthening ancestor worship practices (Gao, 1999; Li, 2007).
2. Responsibilities of the living: The fear of ancestral harm promoted a sense of responsibility among the living to maintain familial lineage and upholding moral values (Chen, 2015; Wang, 2016).
3. Social order and control: The threat of ancestral harm may have served as an effective means of social control, ensuring that people adhered to the power structure and hierarchy in place (Sun, 2008; Zhang, 2013).

Conclusion
Our analysis indicates that while oracle bone inscriptions depict ancestral gods harming their offspring, these events were interpreted by the Shang people through specific cultural and religious lenses. The paper demonstrates that reasons for ancestral harm could include punishment, the influence of other deities, or misinterpretation of natural events. Such beliefs had a significant impact on Shang society, reinforcing the importance of ancestor worship, maintaining strong familial lineage and moral values, and preserving social order. Through a nuanced understanding of these complexities in the Shang Dynasty’s relationship with their ancestors, we are better equipped to appreciate the intricate ties between religion and daily life in ancient China.

Обеспечение соблюдения прав реализуется путем участия представителя ресурса в создаваемых диспутах в качестве независимой стороны. В случае нанесения в ходе сделки материального ущерба Покупателю или Продавцу, вызванного неисполнением обязательств одной из сторон, либо их надлежащим исполнением, Администрация не несет ответственности.
Положения для покупателей

    1. Правила Площадки имеют приоритет перед Правилами Магазина.
    2. Участвуя в сделке, Покупатель соглашается с Правилами Магазина, сделку с которым он заключает.
    3. При возникновении проблем с заказом, Покупатель имеет право открыть диспут в течение 24 часов с момента создания заказа.
    4. Модератор обязан вынести предварительное решение по открытому диспуту не позднее, чем 48 часов после его открытия.
    5. Если второй участник игнорирует запросы Модератора в течение 24 часов, положительное решение выносится в пользу другой стороны.
    6. Средства, потраченные на оплату заказа в случае положительного решения по спору возвращаются на счет Покупателя.
    7. Снятие с баланса возвращенных средств запрещено.
    8. Средства, перечисленные за невыполненный или некачественно выполненный заказ, можно потратить только на оплату других товарных единиц, либо оказываемых услуг, предлагаемых на платформе.
    9. Не подлежат обжалованию сделки, совершенные на других торговых площадках, социальных сетях или мессенджерах. В этом случае администрация вправе не рассматривать иск со стороны Покупателя или Продавца.
    10. В отношении сотрудников площадки запрещены: оскорбления/хамство/унизительные обращения/распространения заведомо ложной информации. В противном случае модератор в праве отказать в рассмотрении проблемы, либо заблокировать пользователя, в том числе магазин.
    11. Модератор имеет право закрыть диспут на основе предоставленных данных, без предоставления фото и дополнительной информации, при сопутствующих климатических, географических, временных и других погрешностях.
    12. Запрещено манипулировать правилами ресурса в свою пользу. Если в заказе обнаружено нарушение, требуется доказать факт нарушения, пригласить модератора и ожидать проверку. Любой шантаж, манипуляции и провокации в любом диалоге, могут послужить досрочным закрытием спора в противоположную сторону.
    13. Во исполнении контроля за соблюдением Правил Администрация в праве временно отключать от площадки магазины и сервисы, имеющие высокий процент диспутов и жалоб. По факту жалоб производится расследование, по итогам которого Продавец получает штраф за обнаруженные нарушения и предписание исправить их в установленный срок. В случае отказа от выполнения предписания Администрации шоп или сервис получают перманентный бан, а депозит, в случае его наличия, возвращается владельцу после процедуры удержания штрафов и компенсации нанесенного вреда пострадавшим от противоправных действий Продавца, в случае их наличия.
    14. Не запрещено, но не желательно осуществлять за пределами площадки действия, связанные с трудовой деятельностью, как то: найм, рабочее общение, выплаты и прочие возможные предметы споров. В случае вынесения одного из аспектов за пределы площадки, вам может быть отказано в рассмотрении претензий Администрацией. Для внесения залога сотрудник покупает залоговую позицию строго на витрине магазина, в который устравивается и планирует работать.

Title: Reflection on the External Dissemination of Modern Chinese Culture from 1840 to 1949

Abstract

The period between 1840 and 1949 marked a significant change in China’s social, political, and cultural landscape, driving the country to open up to the outside world, both as a consequence and as an intentional course of action. During this time, the external dissemination of modern Chinese culture faced various obstacles and opportunities, which in turn impacted its development and influence on the global stage. This article aims to provide a critical analysis of the factors affecting the external dissemination of modern Chinese culture during this period.

Introduction

The historical period from 1840 to 1949 saw the decline of the Qing dynasty, the rise of the Republic of China, and the establishment of the People’s Republic of China. During this tumultuous time, external forces pushed China to reconsider its traditional cultural norms and values, as well as the means by which it communicated and interacted with the rest of the world. This article examines the challenges and factors influencing the external dissemination of modern Chinese culture within this period.

Section 1: The Challenges of Cultural Dissemination

1.1 Isolationism and its impact on cultural dissemination

The isolationist policies of the late Qing dynasty were a significant barrier to the dissemination of Chinese culture, as various factors – including political influence, economic factors, and the belief in the superiority of Chinese culture – led to a deep-rooted resistance to foreign influence. As a result, the flow of Chinese cultural exports was limited, and the dissemination of modern Chinese culture beyond the country’s borders faced significant obstacles.

1.2 The impact of foreign aggression and cultural imperialism

The Opium Wars and the unequal treaties forced upon China by foreign powers also negatively impacted the dissemination of Chinese culture. The humiliation and oppression suffered by the Chinese people became an inseparable part of modern Chinese cultural consciousness, influencing the way that the culture was perceived and presented to the outside world. This created a sense of cultural defensiveness and an unwillingness to share Chinese culture indiscriminately, thereby impeding its dissemination.

Section 2: Opportunities for Cultural Dissemination

2.1 Intellectual and cultural movements

Significant intellectual and cultural movements arose during this period, such as the May Fourth Movement and the New Culture Movement, which allowed for the creation of new cultural products and ideas that were more appealing to the global audience. These movements sought to transform Chinese culture and adapt it to modern needs, in turn making it more accessible to the international audience.

2.2 The role of overseas Chinese communities

The vast number of Chinese citizens moving overseas, particularly in the wake of foreign aggression, helped to facilitate the dissemination of Chinese culture through establishing cultural exchange within their host countries. The process of cultural integration within these communities provided an avenue for the sharing and promotion of Chinese culture, contributing to greater understanding and appreciation of modern Chinese culture worldwide.

Conclusion

The external dissemination of modern Chinese culture during the period from 1840 to 1949 was influenced by a complex interplay of historical, social, and political factors. While it faced significant challenges in terms of isolationism and foreign aggression, opportunities arose through intellectual and cultural movements and the influence of overseas Chinese communities. Understanding this historical context is crucial for appreciating the role of China in global cultural development during this period, and its long-lasting impact on contemporary Chinese culture.

One of the most prominent aspects of Shang religion was the worship of local deities, also known as “diqi.” This paper will analyze the ways in which the Shang Dynasty expressed their worship of these local deities, based on the evidence found in oracle bone inscriptions.

I. Assimilation of Local Deities
A. Incorporating Ancestors into Diqi System
B. Ancestral Worship in Shang Religion
C. Examples of Ancestral Worship in Oracle Bone Inscriptions

II. Sacrificial Rites for Local Deities
A. Importance of Sacrifice in Shang Religion
B. Food and Pleasure as Means to Personify Diqi
C. Examples of Sacrificial Rites in Oracle Bone Inscriptions

III. Appeasement of Local Deities
A. Importance of Appeasement in Shang Religion
B. Protection of Mountains and Rivers
C. Prayers for Rain, Drives Away Locusts, and Visits from Ancestors
D. Examples of Appeasement in Oracle Bone Inscriptions

Conclusion: Through an analysis of oracle bone inscriptions, we can see that the Shang Dynasty expressed their worship of local deities by assimilating them into their ancestral system, performing sacrificial rites to personify them, and appeasing them through protective measures and offerings. These practices reflected the Shang’s beliefs in the power and influence that these local deities held over their daily lives.

However, despite this theoretical framework, the translation of peculiar postmodern terms presents a significant challenge. To address this, we propose four different strategies for translating postmodern terminology:

1. Transliteration as a Specific Translation Technique (Direct Translation)

Transliteration is the process of representing a word or phrase from the source language using the closest possible characters in the target language. This approach is particularly useful for translating unique or culture-specific terms that may have no direct equivalent in the target language while maintaining the integrity of the term’s lexical roots. However, it must be used cautiously, as it may result in ambiguities or confusion for the target audience, requiring further contextual explanation or analysis.

2. Modulation as a Polysemous Approach (Oblique Translation)

Modulation involves adjusting the source text’s linguistic and stylistic features in the target language, aiming to achieve a more idiomatic or natural expression while preserving the intended meaning. This method is beneficial when translating postmodern philosophical texts, as it allows the translator to adapt the language to the intricacies of the target language and produce a more accessible and relevant translation. Modulation can be applied to various aspects, including lexical, syntactic, and semantic levels, resulting in a text that resonates with the target audience’s cultural and linguistic norms.

3. Translation Comment as a Way to Explain the Translation (Oblique Translation)

In cases where a direct or modulated translation is insufficient for conveying the intended meaning or nuance of a postmodern term or concept, the translator may opt to include a translation comment. This technique entails providing additional explanations or clarifications within the translated text to ensure that the target audience gains a comprehensive understanding of the original idea. Translation comments may be inserted as footnotes, marginal notes, or explanatory passages in the text, depending on the most suitable format for the specific material.

4. Neologism as a Translation Solution (Oblique Translation)

	One of the challenges in translating postmodern philosophical texts is the frequent use of neologisms or terms unique to the source language’s culture. In such cases, the translator may decide to coin a new term in the target language that accurately captures the semantic, cultural, and intellectual essence of the original term. The creation of neologisms necessitates a deep understanding of both the source and target languages, as well as the cultural, historical, and philosophical contexts involved. While this approach can provide a viable solution for conveying complex concepts, care must be taken to ensure that the new term will be comprehensible and relatable for the target audience

Title: Filial Piety in the Shang Dynasty: Ancestor Worship and Its Three Forms

Abstract: Filial piety is a highly valued virtue in the Chinese culture, and it has been practiced since ancient times. In the Shang Dynasty, ancestor worship was the primary means by which the virtue of filial piety was realized. This paper examines ancestor worship in the Shang Dynasty, focusing on the three forms it takes: asking gods, nurturing gods, and praising gods. This paper presents the historical and cultural background of ancestor worship and analyzes the mechanisms through which ancestor worship enables filial piety to be transmitted and embodied. The paper concludes that ancestor worship in the Shang Dynasty was an essential component of filial piety and that its legacy lived on in Chinese culture.

Introduction:
Filial piety, or xiào (孝), is a fundamental virtue in Chinese culture. The concept of filial piety encompasses respect for one’s parents, grandparents, and ancestors, as well as loyalty to one’s family and society (Liu, 2004). In the Shang Dynasty (1600-1046 BC), ancestor worship was the primary means by which the virtue of filial piety was realized. Ancestor worship takes three forms: asking gods, nurturing gods, and praising gods. This paper examines ancestor worship in the Shang Dynasty and its role in promoting filial piety.

Culture and History of Ancestor Worship in the Shang Dynasty:
Ancestor worship is deeply rooted in Chinese culture and has been practiced since antiquity. In the Shang Dynasty, ancestor worship was a vital aspect of religious and social life (Chen, 2015). It was believed that the spirits of ancestors could communicate with the living and bestow blessings or curses upon their descendants. Ancestors were thus worshipped for their guidance and protection. Ancestor worship was also a means of cementing family ties and preserving family lineage.

Asking Gods: Inquiring About Ancestors’ Opinions:
Asking gods, or xúnshén (询神), was one of the three forms of ancestor worship in the Shang Dynasty. It involved seeking the advice and guidance of ancestors through divination. Divination was conducted using oracle bones, which were bones or tortoise shells inscribed with questions and then heated until they cracked. The cracks were interpreted as a message from the ancestors. Asking gods was an essential means of seeking ancestors’ opinions on family and clan matters (Liu, 2012).

Nurturing Gods: Sacrificing Ancestors:
Nurturing gods, or yangshén (养神), was another form of ancestor worship in the Shang Dynasty. It involved making offerings to ancestors and ensuring their well-being in the afterlife. Ancestors were believed to need nourishment from their descendants in the form of food, wine, and other offerings. Nurturing gods was thus a means of showing gratitude and respect to one’s ancestors.

Praising Gods: Spreading the Reputation of Ancestors Through Texts for Generations:
Praising gods, or sòngshén (颂神), was the third form of ancestor worship in the Shang Dynasty. It involved singing the praises of one’s ancestors and spreading their reputation through texts for generations. Ancestors who had achieved great deeds or had been particularly virtuous were commemorated in songs and stories. Praising gods was thus a means of passing on the virtue and wisdom of ancestors to future generations.

Conclusion:
This paper has examined the three forms of ancestor worship in the Shang Dynasty: asking gods, nurturing gods, and praising gods. We have seen how these three forms of ancestor worship enabled filial piety to be realized and transmitted. Ancestor worship in the Shang Dynasty was a vital aspect of religious and social life and played a significant role in promoting filial piety. Its legacy lived on in Chinese culture, where filial piety remains a highly valued virtue.

Mask R-CNN model setup
Mask R-CNN relies on region proposal networks (RPNs) for identifying objects and is therefore a two-stage detector system. The three main steps (Figure 3) of the model are as follows: An RPN is used to decide where to search to reduce the computational requirements of the overall inference process; the region proposals are transformed by means of classification and creating of bounding boxes; and finally, the creation of segmentation masks, in which the algorithm takes positive regions of interest (ROIs) as input and creates 28 × 28 pixel floating-point value masks, which are then scaled up. For the inference process, the algorithm uses a multitask loss function: L = Lcls + Lbbox + Lmask (He et al., 2017). The developed model is based on a present implementation by Matterport, Inc. and released under an MIT licence, which is itself constructed based on the open-source libraries Keras and TensorFlow. In our study, we started by using weights obtained from the Microsoft Common Objects in COntext (MS COCO) dataset (Lin et al., 2014). However, a preliminary test showed unsatisfactory results caused by the specific domain-related problem of our dataset, that is, the occurrence of small objects. To counter this issue, we modified the anchor scale to values of 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128. We also modified the training anchors per image to values of 64 and 128, allowing for a large number of detected objects. We trained the model for 15 epochs using the stochastic gradient descent (SGD) method with a momentum of 0.9 and starting with a scheduled learning rate to speed up the training process. Furthermore, we compared the training results and training time for the adaptive gradient method with the dynamic bounds of the learning rate (AdaBound) (Luo et al., 2019) and the SGD optimization method. To reduce overfitting, we applied a weight decay since this parameter adds an L2 penalty to the cost, which can effectively lead to smaller model weights. The model runs under the deep learning development framework of TensorFlow and Keras, with an Nvidia 1080 GPU, an Intel® Core™ i7-8700k CPU and 16 GB memory. For model validation purposes, we divided the 200 training maps into a training subset (80% of the images) and a validation subset (20% of the images).

    stop_words = set(['a', 'an', 'the', 'and', 'in', 'of', 'to', 'that', 'is', 'was', 'for', 'with', 'as', 'on', 'at', 'by', 'be', 'it', 'this', 'which', 'or', 'from', 'not', 'but', 'also', 'his', 'her', 'their', 'they', 'i', 'you', 'we', 'he', 'she', 'it', 'me', 'him', 'her', 'us', 'them', 'my', 'your', 'our', 'his', 'her', 'its', 'their', 'yours', 'ours', 'theirs'])

    # Map each word to a tuple of (word, 1), then reduce by key to count the occurrences of each word
    word_counts = words.map(lambda word: (word, 1)).reduceByKey(lambda x, y: x + y)

Over the centuries, the Chinese culture has gone through numerous transformations, but its essence has remained intact. There's also a story that the bell was to be called “Victoria" in honour of Queen Victoria, but the ceremonial speeches went on so long that some joker shouted out “Oh just call it Big Ben and have done with it!" and the name stuck.

The tower was raised as a part of Charles Barry's design for a new palace, after the old Palace of Westminster was destroyed by fire on the night of October 16,1834. It is designed in the Victorian Gothic style, and is 316 feet (96 m) high. Due to ground conditions present since construction, the tower leans slightly to the northwest, by roughly 8.66 inches (220 millimetres).
The clock faces are set in an iron framework 21 feet (7 metres) in diameter, supporting 576 pieces of opal glass, rather like a stained glass window.
Some of the glass pieces may be removed for inspection of the hands. The minute hand is 14 feet (4. 25 m) long and the figures are 2 feet (0.6 m) high.When Parliament is in session, a light shines above the clock face. At night,the four clock faces are illuminated, making it a particularly impressive sight.
UK nationals may climb the clock tower by prior arrangement by calling:020·7219·3000. Visitors from abroad can request a tour by writing at least three months before the scheduled visit to：Clock Tower Tours, Parliamentary Works Services Directorate, 1 Canon Row, London, SW1A 2JN, England.

The Privilege Given to Clients.
There is a special and very important privilege that has been given to clients.
This has been developed over many years, and belongs to them as a matter of
public policy, in order to ensure the proper and efficient running of the system of
justice. This is that a lawyer must not reveal what he or she has been told by the
client in the course of preparing a case, without the client's consent. This is a
privilege given to the clients who are represented by lawyers. If, therefore, a client
admits to his solicitor and barrister
that he has committed the crime of which he is charged, it is their duty to
advise him that he should plead guilty, but they cannot go to the police and tell
them that their client has confessed. If the police approach them and ask for
information, they cannot (without the client's permission) reveal anything - even if
the client has confessed to murder.
The Privilege Given to Lawyers.
Until recently lawyers too enjoyed an important privilege an "immunity
from suit" – meaning that they could not be sued by their clients for negligence in
respect of their conduct of a case in court. They were privileged from legal action
only in respect of work which was done in court; if a lawyer performed his "out of
court" work negligently, giving bad legal advice, preparing a defective contract
or delaying the start of a claim for so long that the court would not allow it to
proceed, the client could take him to court and claim compensation.
This old law has been changed, but the change is a very limited one. The
clients can sue their lawyers in respect of their conduct of a case in court only if it
is a very plain case of neglect and the Court of Appeal has set aside the defendant's
conviction because he was so badly represented at the trial.
